# `get_algo_param`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read one parameter of the active guiding algorithm for an axis.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build matches (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | D |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, guider handler @0x7c240 (64-bit build); GetParamNames for Hysteresis @0xe25b0, Lowpass @0xe3a50, Lowpass2 @0xe4ee0, ResistSwitch @0xe6280 |

Params are an object {axis, name} or an array [axis, name]; axis is ra/x or dec/y. The handler selects the active algorithm for the axis and calls its virtual parameter getter. The result is the parameter value as a double. Parameter names per algorithm (READ) are hysteresis {hysteresis, aggression, minMove}; lowpass {slopeWeight, minMove}; lowpass2 {aggressiveness, minMove}; resist-switch {aggression, fastSwitch, minMove}. minMove is in pixels (INFERRED). Limits (64-bit; 32-bit not checked; READ) are hysteresis.hysteresis 0..1; hysteresis.aggression above 0 up to 2; lowpass2.aggressiveness 0 or more, no upper limit; resist-switch.aggression above 0 up to 1 (a fraction, not scaled); resist-switch.minMove above 0; every other minMove and lowpass.slopeWeight 0 or more; fastSwitch is never rejected (non-zero means on). The method is registered in the guider command table (TCP 4400); a request that reaches the main imager and is relayed to the guider is a separate route with its own side effects, outside this entry's tier.

Side effects: None established for the handler itself; the algorithm getter is a virtual call whose target set is not closed.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_algo_param"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array | no | - | Axis and parameter name, either as an object {axis, name} or as a positional array [axis, name]. Both strings are required; a missing or non-string member gives error 105. Scalars are not bound. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | axis or name missing or not a string | `expected string param` |
| 323 | The algorithm getter failed (for example an unknown name) | `could not get param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request is not an object, is an empty object, or has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: no method of type string (a non-string method counts as missing) | `invalid request` |
| 101 | Dispatcher: text fails to parse | `invalid JSON request: <reason> on line <n> ...` |
| 103 | Dispatcher: unregistered method | `method not found` |

Out-of-range values are rejected by the algorithm setters (set_algo_param, 322), which then apply and persist a substitute value; see set_algo_param for the limits.

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":5,"method":"get_algo_param","params":{"axis":"ra","name":"aggression"}}
```

Request, request-array:

```json
{"id":6,"method":"get_algo_param","params":["dec","minMove"]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_algo_param","result":80,"code":0,"id":5}
```

Reply, error-323:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_algo_param","error":"could not get param","code":323,"id":7}
```
